statement: For every f,D: R -> R and x,h,L in R, if h>0, L>=0, f is continuous on [x,x+h], f has derivative D(t) at every t in (x,x+h), and |D(t)-D(x)| <= L|t-x| throughout that open interval, then |(f(x+h)-f(x))/h-D(x)| <= Lh. The quotient is precisely Research.forwardDifference(f,x,h). D(x) is the value of the independently quantified function D; no derivative of f at x is assumed.

targets.name: Research.forwardDifference_error_bound
targets.statement: For every pair of functions f,D: R -> R and every x,h,L in R, assume 0<h, 0<=L, and f is continuous on the closed interval [x,x+h]. Assume also that for every real t satisfying x<t<x+h, f has ordinary real derivative D(t) at t, and that for every real t satisfying x<t<x+h, |D(t)-D(x)| <= L|t-x|. Then |Research.forwardDifference(f,x,h)-D(x)| <= Lh, equivalently |(f(x+h)-f(x))/h-D(x)| <= Lh. The derivative is taken for f on R at each interior point. There is no endpoint differentiability hypothesis. The condition on D compares each interior value only with D(x), rather than bounding differences for arbitrary pairs of points.

constructions.name: Research.forwardDifference
constructions.description: A function (R -> R) -> R -> R -> R, defined for every f: R -> R and x,h in R by Research.forwardDifference(f,x,h)=(f(x+h)-f(x))/h. It evaluates f at x+h and x, subtracts f(x) from f(x+h), and divides by h. It performs no limit or derivative operation. The definition requires neither regularity of f nor nonzero h; formal real division is total and gives value 0 when h=0. The target theorem applies this construction only for h>0.

assumptions: R carries its usual real arithmetic, order, absolute value, and topology. Both f and D have domain R and codomain R; x,h,L and each quantified t are real.
The target universally quantifies f,D,x,h,L and assumes h>0 and L>=0.
For every real t in (x,x+h), f has derivative D(t) at t.
For every real t in (x,x+h), |D(t)-D(x)| <= L|t-x|.
No hypothesis asserts differentiability of f at either endpoint, identifies D(x) with a derivative of f at x, requires continuity of D, or imposes a Lipschitz bound between arbitrary pairs of points.
